texts.preamble: M/S Himachal Trading Company vs State Of H.P & Others on 1 September, 2016 Author: Chander Bhusan Barowalia Bench: Chander Bhusan Barowalia In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla Cr.MMO No.78 of 2016. Reserved on :23.8.2016. . Decided on: 1st September, 2016. M/s Himachal Trading Company, Hamirpur. ...Petitioner. Versus State of H.P & Others. ...Resp Coram of The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Chander Bhusan Barowalia, Judge.
texts.facts: Code of Criminal Procedure (for short 'Code') has been preferred by the petitioner for quashing the impugned order dated 29th August, 2013 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Court No.II, Hamirpur, District Hamirpur, H.P, in Complaint No.27-III/2007/118- 1-2009, whereby application under Section 20-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, has been allowed and the petitioner has been ordered to be summoned and impleaded as accused No.2. Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment? Yes. 2. Brief facts giving rise to the present petition are that respondent No.1/Food Inspector, Hamirpur, filed a complaint under . Section 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hamirpur, the same was assigned to the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Court No.II, of Hamirpur, for disposal in accordance with law. It is alleged in the complaint that on 5th March, 2007 at about 1:00 pm, respondent rt No.1/Food Inspector, inspected the shop of respondent No.2 and found ten original sealed packets of "Vanaspati Ghee" for sale to the General Public with mark DO Khajoor manufactured by Bhatinda Chemical Limited, Hazi Road, Bhatinda, weighing 1000 ml. Thereafter, respondent No.1 associated the witnesses of sample process to take the sample of Ghee from respondent No.2 and issued notice on Form No.7, which was duly signed by respondent No.2. It is further alleged that respondent No.1 purchased three original sealed packets each of 100 ml;. of "Vansapati Ghee" from respondent No.2 on payment of `189/-, against proper receipt issued by respondent No.2 and signed by the witnesses. After completing all the codal formalities, the sample was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst, Kandaghat, who found the same to be adulterated, as per the report submitted by him. Respondent No.1 obtained sanction from the competent authority to initiate the prosecution against respondent No.2. The complaint was filed on 19th November, 2007 and on receipt thereof, notice was issued to . respondent No.2, who moved an application under Section 13 (ii) of the Act, for sending the sealed sample which was sealed by Food Inspector and sent to the Public Analyst, Mysore, the report was received by the learned Court, same was different from the report of submitted by the Public Analyst, Kandaghat. Notice of Accusation was put to respondent No.2/accused, who pleaded not guilty and rt claimed trial. After leading the prosecution evidence, defence was recorded and an application under Section 20-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, was moved on behalf of respondent No.2 for impleading present petitioner, as co-accused, on the ground that he had purchased the same from the present petitioner. The application was not contested by the complainant. The same was allowed, vide order dated 29.8.2013 and the petitioner was impleaded, as co-accused, with respondent No.2. 3. The petitioner has assailed his impleadment on the ground that the learned Court below has not applied proper mind and not come to the conclusion after going through the evidence and conducting proper inquiry that the petitioner is a necessary party. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has argued that the petitioner was neither necessary nor proper party, . as there is no evidence against the petitioner and the impugned order passed by the learned Court below is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. He has further argued that the learned Court below has not conducted any inquiry with respect to the involvement of the of petitioner and simply made petitioner, as accused, vide order dated 29.8.2013. 6. rt Learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 has argued that there is no illegality and irregularity in the impugned order passed by the learned Court below, therefore, the present petition is not maintainable. 7. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.3 has argued that there was ample evidence on record to implead the petitioner/applicant as respondent, as he has sold the sealed material to the petitioner and the impugned order passed by the learned Court below suffers from no illegality. 8. In rebuttal, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has argued that the petitioner has not manufactured the material, which is evident from the record. 9.
